turns.question: How do I add DocPilot to a Vue app?
turns.gold_answer: Install `@cloflin/docpilot`, import `@cloflin/docpilot/style/core.css`, and register `DocPilotPlugin` from `@cloflin/docpilot/vue` with `config: __DOCPILOT__`, your `router`, and optionally `highlighter: createShikiHighlighter()` (whose four `@shikijs/*` packages you install yourself). Then place `<DocPilotIcons />` once, `<DocPilotTrigger />` wherever a button belongs, and `<DocPilot />` once — it teleports. `__DOCPILOT__` comes from `define: { __DOCPILOT__: JSON.stringify(ai.themeConfig) }` in `vite.config.js`, with `ai = defineDocPilot(docPilot, process.env)`.

turns.question: And for a React app instead?
turns.gold_answer: Import `DocPilotPanel` from `@cloflin/docpilot/react` and `@cloflin/docpilot/web.css`, and render `<DocPilotPanel config={window.__DOCPILOT__} route={pathname} />` once in your layout. The component renders one empty `div` and teleports everything visible to the body. It imports the prebuilt `@cloflin/docpilot/web` bundle, so the app needs no Vue, no loader and no configuration, and that bundle installs Shiki itself. Pass `route` and `lang` as props and change them on navigation; the panel does not remount.

turns.question: How does the route I pass relate to my site's base path and to the citations?
turns.gold_answer: `route` is base-less — `/guide/install`, not `/docs/guide/install`; a site served from a subdirectory says so once with `base="/docs/"`. `base` is applied at exactly two points, the index fetch and following a citation; routes and citation hrefs are base-less everywhere, which is what lets the citation validator compare them literally. A page's route is its path under `docsDir` with `.md` dropped and a trailing `index` collapsed, and it has to be the URL your site actually serves, or citations 404.

turns.question: What does that validator actually check?
turns.gold_answer: Before an answer renders, its citations are compared against the set of chunk ids the host put in front of the model that turn; an id the model invented is stripped with its marker, and surviving markers renumber. Links are checked against the page set in the token stream, and an invented route is de-linked and left as plain text. An answer with no surviving citations is not shown — it becomes a refusal.

turns.question: How do I stop the panel from storing readers' conversations?
turns.gold_answer: Set `history: { enabled: false }`. It stops recording and also clears what is already stored, on the reader's next visit, so a site that turns it off leaves nothing behind. It covers the half-typed draft (`composer.draft`) and `history.saveOnUnload` too.

turns.question: How do I make the panel use my brand font?
turns.gold_answer: The panel ships no font of its own: `--dp-font` is `inherit`, and on VitePress and Docusaurus the adapter maps it to the host's own family. To name one for the whole site, set `ui: { font: '--brand-font' }` — a bare `--name` is wrapped into `var(--name)` — or a family list such as `'Inter, system-ui, sans-serif'`. When the value depends on something only a stylesheet knows, override the token in CSS instead: `:root { --dp-font: var(--my-font); }`.

turns.question: Now do the same for the code blocks.
turns.gold_answer: Use `ui.fontMono` beside it, e.g. `ui: { font: '--brand-font', fontMono: 'JetBrains Mono, monospace' }`, or override `--dp-font-mono` in CSS. It covers the code blocks, the reasoning trace and the prompt disclosure. It has no `inherit` default and should not be given one: a page has no monospace face to borrow, so unset it keeps a system monospace stack.

turns.question: How does that setting interact with the VitePress adapter's own font?
turns.gold_answer: `ui.font` and `ui.fontMono` are written onto `<html>` as inline custom properties `--dp-font` and `--dp-font-mono`, which is the only layer that outranks an adapter, so the value reaches the panel on VitePress and Docusaurus too. Without it, the VitePress adapter maps `--dp-font` to `var(--vp-font-family-base)` and `--dp-font-mono` to `var(--vp-font-family-mono)`. A `:root` rule of your own beats the adapter only if it is loaded after it.

turns.question: Why does my :root rule have to be loaded after the adapter?
turns.gold_answer: Because order is the mechanism, not a convention. The core declares every token with a real value; the adapter re-declares the set on `:root` at the same specificity and wins by coming second. A `:root` rule of yours has that same specificity, so it wins only by coming later. An adapter loaded first loses, and loaded alone it gives the panel no styles at all.

turns.question: How many requests does one question cost on the free tier?
turns.gold_answer: A turn is one embedding request plus one or more model calls: a one-shot turn is 1 embed + 1 model call, an agentic turn is 1 embed + 2–3 model calls, plus any the pool rotates through. A follow-up's two query texts ride a single embedding request. `embed: false` makes no embedding request, which roughly doubles the one-shot questions a day, at the cost of the dense retrieval channel.

turns.question: Как запустить панель на бесплатном тарифе OpenRouter?
turns.gold_answer: Достаточно `chat: { provider: 'openrouter' }` без названия модели и ключа `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`: чат получает `openrouter/free` — собственный роутер OpenRouter по бесплатному тарифу, который сам выбирает свободную модель на каждый запрос и пропускает перегруженные. Бесплатный тариф ограничивает запросы в день, а не токены: 50 в день при покупке меньше 10 кредитов, 1000 — от 10 кредитов, и всегда 20 в минуту. Окно заканчивается в полночь UTC.

turns.question: А теперь сделай так, чтобы браузер сам перебирал пул из десяти моделей.
turns.gold_answer: Назовите пул явно: `chat: { provider: 'openrouter', model: 'free' }`. Это упорядоченный пул из десяти: впереди `openrouter/free`, за ним девять явных бесплатных id. Если одна модель отказывает, отвечает следующая, а отказавшая уходит в конец списка на минуту; ответившая пробуется первой на следующем ходу. С версии 1.4.0 молчание больше не означает этот пул.

turns.question: Как это взаимодействует с бюджетом?
turns.gold_answer: Когда в дне остаётся `budget.rotateAbove` (по умолчанию 6) ответов или меньше, пул перестаёт перебираться; при `budget.oneShotBelow` (15) и ниже ходы становятся one-shot — один запрос вместо трёх-четырёх. Эти правила включаются только на счёте, который можно защитить: на заданном `budget.dailyLimit` или на известном потолке поставляемого бесплатного пула. `budget: false` выключает все правила.

turns.question: Что значит one-shot — что я при этом теряю?
turns.gold_answer: One-shot — это один запрос к модели на весь вопрос: потолок итераций сводится к 0, и управление сразу переходит к финальному вызову, который уже несёт первичную выдачу, строгую схему ответа и набор для цитирования. Ответ уже, но не испорчен: модель не может сначала поискать дополнительные свидетельства. Он так же хорош, как первая выдача, зато даёт примерно втрое больше вопросов в день.

turns.question: Как сделать панель шире?
turns.gold_answer: Переопределите геометрический токен `--dp-width` после таблицы стилей, например `:root { --dp-width: 520px; }`. По умолчанию он равен `clamp(360px, 30vw, 460px)` и намеренно одинаков для выдвижной панели и попапа.

turns.question: How do I make the panel refuse questions my docs don't cover before the model is called?
turns.gold_answer: Set `guard.mode` to `'calibrated'`. The default since 1.3 is `'off'`: the floor is scored and recorded on every turn, but every question reaches the model. `'dense-only'` refuses only where a dense channel scored it. Run `npx docpilot calibrate` first, because the thresholds are a statement about one corpus and one language; until it has run, provisional values are used and records report `source: "provisional"`.

turns.question: Write that out as the full guard object.
turns.gold_answer: `guard: { mode: 'calibrated', tau: null, tauLexical: null, supportMinIdentifiers: 3 }` — this restores the pre-1.3 refusal contract on every deployment shape. Leave `tau` and `tauLexical` null: `npx docpilot calibrate` writes them into `${evalDir}/calibration.json` and `npx docpilot index` inlines them into the manifest. A hand-set value overrides the measurement and stamps `gate.source: "config"` on every record.

turns.question: How does that interact with follow-ups like "and for backend calls?"
turns.gold_answer: A follow-up like that retrieves nothing on its own, so the gate scores the maximum of the raw question and the question composed with the previous one, which can only reduce refusals. Admissibility stops it being a free pass: at least one content word of the tail must appear in the retrieved evidence — `and for backend calls?` passes, `and for AWS S3 buckets?` does not. The composition uses the last answered question, reaches one turn further back only when that turn was itself an ellipsis, and stops at two.

turns.question: What did you mean by admissibility?
turns.gold_answer: It is the check that at least one content word of the follow-up's tail appears in the retrieved evidence, measured against the reader's own words. Where it cannot be measured — no tail word is known to the corpus and the tail's letters are not the corpus's letters — it stands aside and the dense channel decides alone, still having to beat the raw score and clear the threshold. A topic switch written in the corpus's own script keeps the veto.

turns.question: How do I mount the panel in a React app?
turns.gold_answer: Import `DocPilotPanel` from `@cloflin/docpilot/react` and `@cloflin/docpilot/web.css`, then render `<DocPilotPanel config={window.__DOCPILOT__} route={pathname} />` once; it renders one empty `div` and teleports the panel to the body. It uses the prebuilt web bundle, so no Vue is needed. Pass `route` and `lang` as props and change them on navigation — the panel does not remount.

turns.question: How are the vectors stored in the built index?
turns.gold_answer: As one sign bit per dimension when the embedder is wide enough — a thirty-second of float32 — in a single `vectors.<hash>.bin` blob of exactly `chunkCount × dims / 8` bytes; the question's vector is never quantised. The browser scores `Σ q[i] · sign(d[i])` and multiplies once by a corpus-wide `cosScale` from the manifest. With the default `--quantize=auto` the bit is written only when the measured error is at most `0.015`, otherwise int8; above `0.03` the build dies.

turns.question: Give me the commands to compare that against int8 on my own corpus.
turns.gold_answer: Build each format and run the eval after each build: `npx docpilot index --quantize=int8 && npx docpilot eval --gate-only`, then `npx docpilot index --quantize=binary && npx docpilot eval --gate-only`. Both runs share one index hash, so compare the timestamped copies in `${evalDir}/reports/history/`, not `latest.json`.

turns.question: How does switching that format interact with the gate's calibrated thresholds?
turns.gold_answer: The fitted `cosScale` keeps the dense score on the cosine scale that the gate and its calibrated thresholds are written in. But a threshold calibrated on one format is a measurement of that format, so re-run `calibrate` after the format changes. On this site, after re-calibration on the 1-bit index, `tau` moved from 0.55 to 0.57.

turns.question: What do you mean that cosScale is fitted?
turns.gold_answer: It is one corpus-wide number that the build fits by least squares and writes into the manifest. The browser computes the asymmetric product `Σ q[i] · sign(d[i])` between the full-precision question vector and the chunk sign bits, then multiplies it once by `cosScale`, which puts the dense score back on the cosine scale. Every build also samples up to 200 vector pairs and prints the mean `|Δcos|` against the exact float cosine.

turns.question: How do I install the skills for Cursor instead of Claude Code?
turns.gold_answer: Run `npx docpilot init --target=cursor` (a comma list such as `--target=claude,cursor` works). With `--scope=project` the skills go to `.cursor/skills/` and the slash commands to `.cursor/commands/`; `--scope=user` uses `~/.cursor/skills/` and `~/.cursor/commands/`. After a package upgrade, `npx docpilot update` refreshes them.

turns.question: Where does the panel keep a reader's past conversations?
turns.gold_answer: On the reader's own device, under your site's origin, and never sent anywhere. The archive is `docpilot:history` in `localStorage`, shared by every tab; `docpilot:conversation` in `sessionStorage` records which conversation this tab shows; `docpilot:draft` in `sessionStorage` holds the half-typed question, redacted. The list opens from the clock button in the panel header.

turns.question: Now give me the config that keeps only 5 of them and drops the export button.
turns.gold_answer: `history: { enabled: true, maxConversations: 5, exportThread: false }`. The default is `{ enabled: true, maxConversations: 20, exportThread: true }`. `maxConversations` is the length of the list — the oldest falls off the end, with a byte ceiling of a tenth of `localStorage` underneath — and `exportThread` is the header button that copies the whole conversation as Markdown.

turns.question: How does a reopened conversation handle a follow-up if the retrieved excerpts aren't stored?
turns.gold_answer: A follow-up asked in a reopened conversation is primed with the sections the previous answer cited — up to three — because their addresses are recovered from the stored source rows and fetched again from the current index; a section that has left the corpus since is dropped rather than trusted. The model also gets conversation memory: three question–answer pairs, questions verbatim and answers condensed to a skeleton within 360 characters.

turns.question: Why would a section be dropped?
turns.gold_answer: Because the index may have been rebuilt since the conversation, and a section that has left the corpus is dropped rather than trusted. Rebuilding does not throw the archive away: an older conversation still opens with the notice "The docs have changed since this conversation. Some links may no longer work.", and answers are re-rendered against the current index, so links to deleted pages come back de-linked.

turns.question: What cache headers should the index files be served with?
turns.gold_answer: `manifest.json` is unhashed and served `no-cache`; `chunks-NN.<hash>.json`, `df.<hash>.json` and `vectors.<hash>.bin` carry a content hash and are `immutable`, which makes a deploy atomic for the browser. Leave `vectors.bin` out of `gzip_types` — it is already quantised — and make sure nothing in front of the host transforms it.

turns.question: Как поменять приветствие пустой панели на русской версии сайта?
turns.gold_answer: Через `i18n.locales.ru.translations`: `i18n: { locales: { ru: { translations: { empty: { heading: 'Чем помочь?' } } } } }`. Внутренняя форма побайтно совпадает с i18n локального поиска VitePress; внешний ключ — `i18n`, а не `locales`, потому что у конфига VitePress уже есть верхний `locales`. Переопределение одной строки сохраняет остальные: слияние идёт по листьям, а не по блокам.

turns.question: А теперь добавь туда ещё плейсхолдер поля ввода.
turns.gold_answer: Добавьте в тот же блок `ru` группу `composer`: `i18n: { locales: { ru: { translations: { empty: { heading: 'Чем помочь?' }, composer: { placeholderNoProduct: 'Спросите про документацию' } } } } }`. Остальные строки группы `composer` сохраняют значения по умолчанию.

turns.question: Как это связано с языком, на котором читатель пишет вопрос?
turns.gold_answer: В панели два селектора. UI-локаль задаётся локалью страницы (`lang`) и покрывает все кнопки, подписи, статусы и отказы — в том числе `empty` и `composer`. Локаль ответа — это язык, на котором читатель напечатал вопрос, и она покрывает только `reply.credential.*` и `reply.social.*`. Какой селектор у ключа — свойство ключа, а не настройка; оба селектора — субтеги, так что один блок `ru` покрывает и интерфейс, и ответы.

turns.question: Что ты имел в виду под reply.* — откуда они берутся, если я их не перевёл?
turns.gold_answer: Это две копии, которые хост пишет без вызова модели: предупреждение об учётных данных (`reply.credential.*`) и ответы на приветствие (`reply.social.*`) — группа `reply` из 15 ключей. В отличие от остального интерфейса, они поставляются на восемнадцати языках. Для `reply.*` цепочка отката особая: после `i18n.locales[селектор]` и `i18n.translations` берётся блок локали страницы, затем поставляемое значение для локали, затем `en`. Региональный тег нормализуется: `ru-RU` находит `ru`.

turns.question: Как подключить DocPilot к сайту на Docusaurus?
turns.gold_answer: Установите `@cloflin/docpilot`, задайте в `docpilot.config.mjs` `indexDir: 'static/rag'` (Docusaurus раздаёт `static/`, а не `public/`) и выполните `npx docpilot index` и `npx docpilot calibrate`. В `docusaurus.config.js` добавьте `plugins: [['@cloflin/docpilot/docusaurus', { config: ai.themeConfig }]]`, где `ai = defineDocPilot(docPilot, process.env)`. Плагин монтирует панель и её две таблицы стилей, инлайнит конфиг как `window.__DOCPILOT__` и держит область «эта страница» в такт с роутером.

turns.question: How do I check in CI that the panel will actually render?
turns.gold_answer: Run `npx docpilot doctor`. It prints what was resolved and either confirms the panel will render or lists what is missing, each with the command or variable that fixes it. It exits non-zero when not ready — the build never fails for these, so `doctor` is the opt-in place to gate CI. It also prints the provider chain with the answering member marked, and only ever the names of variables, never their values.

turns.question: Make that read a boolean in the script instead of the exit code.
turns.gold_answer: Use `npx docpilot doctor --json | jq .ready`. `--json` puts one object on stdout — the same facts the rows carry, plus the installed `version` and `ready` as a boolean — while the diagnosis still goes to stderr. The exit code is unchanged: `ready` and the code are one verdict.

turns.question: How does that relate to free model ids getting retired?
turns.gold_answer: `npx docpilot doctor --models` asks the provider's live free catalogue whether the model list in force — the shipped free pool, or your own `chat.models` — is still served, for the chat and embed halves separately. It prints the pool size against the catalogue size, then `RETIRED:` for every id upstream no longer lists and up to six new ones. The exit code stays the readiness one: a retired id is news, not a broken configuration.

turns.question: Why is that a separate flag and not part of the default run?
turns.gold_answer: Because it is the only thing in `doctor` that touches the network. `doctor` is the command CI gates on, and a check that fails when a third party is slow is a check that gets removed — which takes the readiness gate with it. An unreachable catalogue is printed as unreachable rather than turned into a verdict.

turns.question: Which provider does the panel use when I name none?
turns.gold_answer: `chat.provider` ships as `'auto'`, which walks an ordered list and stops at the first service a key is set for — `openai` (`OPENAI_API_KEY`) first, then `gemini`, `mistral` and the rest; that service's default model comes with it, and `embed: 'auto'` follows it. Providers that embed come first. With nothing set, it falls through to OpenRouter's free tier, `openrouter/free`. A provider you name is never overridden by the environment.
